neighbours.label: the comma that closes a 'no matter what / whatever' concessive clause
fire: No matter how hard the exam looks, you should stay calm.
We keep a spare key outside because, no matter what happens, someone can get in.
Whatever flavor you choose for the cake, use fresh butter.
No matter which route you take, the drive is about two hours.
However late you arrive tonight, please text me first.
No matter where you live in the city, buses run every ten minutes.
Whichever plan you pick in the end, the price includes support.
No matter how many times I explain it, he forgets.
quiet: Because the exam looks hard, you should study early.
We keep a spare key outside because sometimes someone forgets theirs.
When you bake the cake for the party, use fresh butter.
If you take the coast road, the drive is about two hours.
When you arrive tonight, please text me first.
In most parts of the city, buses run every ten minutes.
Since you picked the basic plan, the price includes support.
After I explained it twice, he finally understood.

notes: Card: ',' and '.\n' dominate both poles; probe: 'No matter what ... ,' 0.38, 'Regardless what ... ,' 0.13, other commas <0.1. Narrow guess, low confidence.
